# ar-1 -- the site access point (#30).
#
# interface is the real radio, moved into this container's own network
# namespace by the "interfaces" list in this recipe. It is a netdev
# passthrough, not a USB device passthrough: a wireless adapter is
# claimed by its driver on the host, and what a container needs is the
# resulting interface, not the USB endpoint (daemon/src/device.c says
# so in as many words).
#
# bridge is the whole reason ADR-0264 exists. hostapd puts wlan0 into
# br0 and will create br0 if it is missing -- but it knows nothing
# about this container's other interfaces and would never enslave one,
# so a bridge hostapd built alone would carry the radio and nothing
# else. Cix builds br0 first, with the access-network veth already in
# it, and hostapd then adds the radio to the bridge it finds. Wireless
# clients and the wired access segment are one layer-2 domain.
#
# ctrl_interface is what the hostapd_cli console attaches to.
#
interface=wlan0
bridge=br0
driver=nl80211
ctrl_interface=/run/hostapd

#
# REGULATORY DOMAIN -- confirm this before the AP is used in anger.
#
# country_code decides which channels and powers are legal, and it is
# the one setting in this file that is a legal question rather than a
# technical one. GB is a placeholder chosen from the site's own domain
# (git.uk.home.arpa), which is an inference and not a measurement.
#
# It is also load-bearing beyond legality: with ieee80211d/ieee80211h
# on, cfg80211 applies the regulatory database (wireless-regdb, shipped
# in the cix-firmware image) for this country, and an AP asking for a
# channel that country does not allow simply fails to start.
#
country_code=GB
ieee80211d=1
ieee80211h=1

#
# Band and channel.
#
# 5 GHz, channel 36. The adapter is an RTL8822BU -- 802.11ac dual-band
# -- and channel 36 is the bottom of UNII-1, which is non-DFS in every
# common domain. A DFS channel would make the AP wait out a radar scan
# before it ever beacons, which is a poor thing to debug a first
# bring-up through.
#
# For 2.4 GHz instead, this becomes: hw_mode=g, channel=6, and drop the
# three vht lines. Worth knowing because rtw88's USB AP support is the
# open question this container exists to answer, and if 5 GHz AP mode
# is not supported, 2.4 GHz is the next thing to try rather than a
# rebuild.
#
hw_mode=a
channel=36
ieee80211n=1
ieee80211ac=1
vht_oper_chwidth=0
vht_oper_centr_freq_seg0_idx=36

#
# The network itself.
#
# WPA2-PSK with CCMP only. TKIP is not offered at all -- it is broken,
# and offering it as a fallback is how a network ends up negotiating it.
#
# The passphrase below is a secret placeholder in the committed
# recipe, substituted from the apply request rather than stored here.
# This file is in git; the passphrase is not, and never will be.
#
# The placeholder is deliberately not spelled out in this comment:
# cixd warns when a RENDERED container still contains the token prefix,
# and prose describing it trips that check exactly as a forgotten
# secret would. A warning that cries wolf at documentation is worse
# than no warning.
#
ssid=cix
wpa=2
wpa_key_mgmt=WPA-PSK
rsn_pairwise=CCMP
wpa_passphrase={{SECRET:WIFI_PASSPHRASE}}

# Clients talk to each other through the bridge, which is what a normal
# wireless LAN does. Set to 1 to isolate them from one another.
ap_isolate=0
